findings_addressed: FIX-1 [P2] 1/1 — A DECLARATION ATTACHED TO EVERY LOCKED VERSION OF ITS NAME (scripts/sbom-survey/sbom_survey/survey.py). `_Assembler.add_declarations` looked a declaration up by (ecosystem, name) and attached the origin, the `fathomdb:constraint` and `direct`-ness to EVERY locked entry carrying that name. The moment a lockfile holds two versions of one package that is false, and it was false three times on this repository: `sha2 0.10.9` carried `constraint='0.11'` (0.11 cannot resolve to 0.10.9); `thiserror 2.0.18` was `direct` under `1`; `tokenizers 0.22.2` was `direct` under `0.20`. `depth` and `edit_sites` are the two fields Slice 33 makes its surgical/not-surgical call on, so this corrupted the output the tool exists to produce. CLOSED by a new `sbom_survey/constraints.py` — `matches(ecosystem, constraint, version) -> bool | None`, PEP 440 via `packaging` and semver ranges (^, ~, >=, >, <=, <, =, bare, `||`, hyphen ranges, x-wildcards, and cargo's bare-is-caret versus npm's bare-is-exact) via `semver.Version`. NO NEW DEPENDENCY: both distributions were already declared in the tool's own pyproject.toml for exactly these jobs (§5.7). `add_declarations` now has three cases: no lock entry -> unchanged (unresolved component); exactly ONE candidate -> unchanged and deliberately so, since there is no ambiguity to resolve and no imperfection in the range grammar can therefore regress a correct attachment; several candidates -> attach ONLY to the entries the constraint admits. Applied to all three arms, not just cargo.

FIX-1 — NEVER FABRICATE, NEVER SILENTLY WIDEN. `matches()` returns `None` — not `False` and not `True` — for anything outside its grammar (`workspace:*`, git URLs, `file:` paths, npm aliases, `workspace`/`path`/`git` placeholders, unparseable versions). When a constraint admits NONE of several candidates, or could not be evaluated at all, the declaration is NOT widened back onto every candidate: THAT FALLBACK IS THE DEFECT. It lands instead on an unresolved component that records WHY, so the manifest still appears in `edit_sites` (a real declaration is never silently dropped) while no locked version is falsely claimed to satisfy it. The reason surfaces twice: `fathomdb:resolution-note` in the BOM, and the staleness row's `lookup_error` — the field §5.8 already designates for 'why is this row unknown', so no new row field was needed and the FROZEN 11-field Slice-33 contract is untouched. `lookup_error` reasons now ACCUMULATE rather than overwrite, and a resolution note deliberately does NOT suppress a good `latest` (only a genuine lookup failure does), so the two concerns stay separable.

TC-97 — THE PYTEST HEADER NOW PRINTS `configfile:`, AND IT IS NOT A LEAK. The mechanism is explicit in the installed pytest source (_pytest/config/findpaths.py::locate_config): a pyproject.toml carrying no [tool.pytest.ini_options] makes load_config_dict_from_file return None, and the function then falls through to `if found_pyproject_toml is not None: return found_pyproject_toml.parent, found_pyproject_toml, {}, []` — i.e. the file becomes the ROOTDIR ANCHOR with an EMPTY config dict. src/python/pyproject.toml is not on the ancestor chain and is never reached. NO [tool.pytest.ini_options] table was added, and no pyproject.toml / pytest.ini / tox.ini / setup.cfg was created above scripts/sbom-survey/. TC-105 / §7 BOUNDARY-DEFECT SWEEP — 'a criterion graded against a helper while the integration boundary that must call it goes ungraded' produced 9 of Slice 31's 12 review findings. Slice 32 is the mirror image of that: an implementation can satisfy a helper's contract while the boundary does not do the thing. EVERY ITEM the prompt listed was swept, and each was verified TWICE — once by reading/writing the code, and once EMPIRICALLY by deliberately breaking it and confirming the frozen suite goes RED (the 14-mutation sweep below). (1) run_survey takes its manifests ONLY from discover_manifests(): grep across scripts/sbom-survey/sbom_survey/ for os.walk / rglob / iglob / glob. / import glob / .iterdir() / scandir returns ONLY docstring and comment hits, and there is no literal 'python/' path in code. (2) run_survey calls published.latest() ONCE PER COMPONENT — instrumented a counting source over the real repo: 773 components, 773 calls, 704 distinct (ecosystem, name) keys. (3) Exclusion and tiering come ONLY from the injected/loaded TierMap: the string 'dev/release/fixtures/' appears in the repository's code path nowhere — only in tiers.toml (data) and in prose. (4) Tier matching is longest-prefix-wins via max(len(prefix)) over EVERY matching rule, so it is order-independent by construction; two distinct prefixes of equal length cannot both prefix one string, so the winner is unique. Duplicate prefixes raise DuplicateTierPrefixError (a TierRuleFileError/ValueError, deliberately NOT an UntieredManifestError) from load_tier_map(), naming the prefix. (5) The BOM's fathomdb:tier is derived from the DECLARING MANIFEST's rule verdict — independently recomputed over the real repo: 42 components carry exactly one origin, 0 tier mismatches against TierMap.classify(origin).tier. (6) `direct` is DEFINED as 'has at least one tracked declaring manifest', so a direct component with no fathomdb:declared-in origin is impossible by construction — verified: 0 depth/origin contradictions across 773 components. (7) The default timestamp is a fixed epoch produced by ONE function, resolve_timestamp(), shared by run_survey and the CLI; argparse's --now default is None PRECISELY so the parser cannot inject a wall-clock stamp behind the survey's back, and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH keeps working as §5.8's override. There is no datetime.now() / utcnow() / time.time() / date.today() call anywhere in the package. (8) write_reports() PRODUCES the artifact shape rather than projecting a poorer one — mutation M9 proves the criterion bites. (9) sbom_survey.cyclonedx.validate() really runs the schema: it returns None for the emitted document and a diagnostic for the known-invalid control, verified out of band as well as by AC-SBOM-10.

DESIGN AMBIGUITY RESOLVED 1/3 — THE TIER OF A COMPONENT REACHABLE FROM SEVERAL MANIFESTS. §5.3 fixes the tier of a MANIFEST; it does not say what tier a COMPONENT takes when it is declared by more than one manifest, or when it is a transitive with no declaring manifest at all. RESOLUTION, forced by the frozen oracle: a component's tier candidates are the tiers of its DECLARING MANIFESTS when it has any, and otherwise the tiers of the LOCKFILES that resolved it; the highest-priority tier wins (shipped > dev-tooling > eval-only, i.e. TIER_VOCABULARY order). With exactly one origin this reduces to that origin's tier, which is what AC-SBOM-11 requires. NOTE the consequence, stated rather than hidden: `packaging` is both a transitive of the shipped src/python/uv.lock AND a direct dependency of this dev-tooling mini-project, so it tiers dev-tooling. Including the lockfile tier in the candidate set would make it `shipped` and would then FAIL AC-SBOM-11, since it carries exactly one origin. Origins-win is therefore the rule the frozen oracle demands, not a preference.

DESIGN AMBIGUITY 2/3 — WHICH VERSIONS A MANIFEST DECLARATION ATTACHES TO. **SUPERSEDED AT FIX-1; THE ROUND-0 RESOLUTION WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY REPLACED.** §5.5 defines direct-ness by NAME ('the package name appears in a dependency table'), while components are identified per (ecosystem, name, version). At round 0 I resolved that as 'attach the declaration to every component sharing its (ecosystem, name)' and flagged it as a deliberate choice. It is not defensible: where a lockfile carries several versions of one name, it stamps a constraint on versions that constraint cannot resolve to, and it marks them `direct`. codex §9 round 1 caught it and it is the round's single [P2]. THE CORRECTED RESOLUTION: a declaration attaches only to the locked entries its constraint ADMITS, evaluated with the ecosystem's own comparator; a name with exactly one candidate is attached unconditionally (no ambiguity to resolve); and a constraint that admits none — or cannot be evaluated — attaches to none of them and records why on an unresolved component, never widening. WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED from the round-0 entry: pypi names are canonicalized per PEP 503, so a `pyproject.toml` saying `PyYAML` and a lock saying `pyyaml` are one package; and a declared name with NO lock entry anywhere still materializes an UNRESOLVED component (version omitted, purl without an @version segment, `fathomdb:resolution='unresolved'`). That last case is real here — maturin, networkx, numpy, pyyaml, scipy, plus this tool's own cyclonedx-python-lib / packageurl-python / semver — and is exactly the shape test_cyclonedx.py and test_report.py were written to accommodate, which is why `fathomdb:resolution == 'unresolved'` is required by the tests while §5 never spells it out.

LESSON I OWE THE RECORD — FLAGGING AN AMBIGUITY IS NOT CHECKING IT. I identified this exact question at round 0, wrote it up as a resolved ambiguity, and shipped. What I did not do was emit the resulting rows and LOOK at them: one `grep` for names with more than one locked version would have shown `sha2 0.10.9 constraint='0.11'` immediately. My 14-mutation sweep did not help either, because every mutation was derived from what the FROZEN TESTS grade, and the tests do not grade this — so the sweep confirmed the suite bites without ever asking whether the OUTPUT was true. The corrective I applied this round: for a data-producing tool, verify a sample of the produced data against its own semantics, not only the oracle's assertions. The six-row before/after table in this closure exists for that reason.

DESIGN AMBIGUITY RESOLVED 3/3 — THE fathomdb:edge-kind = 'resolved' TAG. §5.5 says lock-derived edges are tagged 'resolved', but CycloneDX `dependencies` entries carry no property bag, so an edge cannot literally hold one. RESOLUTION: the tag is emitted as a COMPONENT property on every component whose outgoing edges came from a lockfile, and the real normal/dev/build kinds — which only manifest-derived declarations carry — travel in staleness.json's `declared_in[].kind`. The §5.5 limitation is thereby recorded rather than papered over.

IMPLEMENTATION CHOICE WORTH FLAGGING — THE DOCUMENT IS BUILT BY THE LIBRARY, NOT HAND-ROLLED. §5.7 makes cyclonedx-python-lib load-bearing twice: to 'build and serialize' the document, and to supply the schema validator. Both uses are taken. sbom_survey/cyclonedx.py assembles a real Bom / Component / Dependency model and serializes with JsonV1Dot6, so the emitted `$schema` / `bomFormat` / `specVersion` / key ordering / dependency array come from the upstream serializer, and the hand-rolled-JSON failure mode REQ-6 exists to prevent is structurally avoided. Determinism was checked against that decision rather than assumed: the serializer sorts components, properties and dependencies, the serialNumber is a UUIDv5 over the sorted bom-ref set (never uuid4), the timestamp is the fixed epoch, and two independent runs are byte-identical.
